The strong<->cluster link. Cluster membership is a property of the Strong's code itself, independent of word_strong/word_registry — deliberately has no FK/dependency on either. `source` tracks provenance (old-system-migration now; future allocation passes get their own source value, never overwriting a prior row in place).

One row per discrete, nameable rule governing the escalation utility itself -- config, not prose (researcher, 2026-08-16 iba-table-review reset). Parallel to cfg_method_rule but scoped to escalation.py, not the debate pipeline.

Alias table mapping the many book abbreviation forms encountered in source data onto a single books row, so that '1Chr', '1Ki' and '1Kgs' all resolve to the same book. 112 aliases cover all 66 books, with the busiest books carrying up to three variants each.

The 66 books of the Bible as canonical reference data: name, testament, canonical order and several code forms used to parse and render verse references. Fully populated and stable — every row was written in a single load on 2026-03-16 and none has been touched since.

The named characteristics belonging to each cluster — the distinct inner-being traits a cluster resolves into, each with a definition. 277 rows across 35 clusters, layered from several eras: 53 backfilled 1:1 from sub-groups in May, and 78 added in July as explicitly PROVISIONAL top-down exemplars. Note that cluster_code has indexes but no foreign key to cluster.

The many-to-many join between a characteristic and the cluster sub-groups that carry it, recording why the pairing holds. In practice it is near 1:1 — 145 distinct sub-groups over 146 rows — and its qualifier notes confirm most rows are single-sub-group representations rather than genuine fan-out.

The 49 top-level thematic groupings of the study (47 M-codes plus FLAG and T2), each naming a domain of the inner life such as Anger, Wisdom or Peace. Keyed on the M-code itself rather than a surrogate id, so the code is the stable identifier used across the cluster tables.

The catalogue-prompted findings layer: one row per observation question asked of a cluster (or of a characteristic, sub-group or verse-context group within it), holding the answer text. At ~20k rows across only 15 clusters it is the bulk output of the pre-reset method, and 1,633 rows are delete-flagged following the 2026-06-11 catalogue restructure.

Write-on-discovery notes made while working a cluster — design rationales, verdicts, synthesis notes and carry-forwards — each addressed to a later phase that should consume it. Unlike cluster_finding these are not prompted by a question; 229 of 276 rows come from the M10 work alone.

Sub-divisions of a cluster (for example M01-A, M01-BOUNDARY), each carrying a label and a core description that scopes which sense of the cluster theme it covers. Only 17 of the 49 clusters have been subdivided, and 19 rows are delete-flagged, so the table records the sub-group design history as well as its live state.

One row per engine or patch execution (875 rows, March to July), recording mode, timing, outcome and roll-up counts of what was written. It is the parent audit record that word_run_state, engine_stream_checkpoint and term_fetch_log hang off, and it logs patch applications as well as engine runs.

Per-stream progress within a run (1,948 rows over 347 runs) — a stream is usually a single term, e.g. 'term:H8637'. It exists to allow resumable, granular progress tracking, and in practice 1,938 of 1,948 streams show complete.

The universal finding store: one row per typed analytical finding, at VERSE, CLUSTER or GLOBAL level, with VERSE dominating (over 430k of 438k rows). The critical fact in the data is that roughly 92% of rows carry delete_flagged=1 — every l2_api and l2_mechanical row and most l2_meaning rows are soft-deleted, leaving only about 35k live findings; the table is therefore mostly a retained legacy substrate rather than an active corpus.

Extracted citations found inside cluster-level narrative text — the pointer that a given cluster_finding or cluster_observation quotes a particular verse, Strong's number, cross-characteristic or verse-context group. Despite the name it does not cite rows in the finding table; its CHECK constraint binds it to cluster_finding and cluster_observation only, and every row was written in a single batch on 3 June 2026.

Joins findings to the observation questions in wa_obs_question_catalogue that they answer — the mechanism by which the question catalogue is scored against the evidence. At 332k rows it is one of the largest tables, but only 31 distinct questions are ever linked, so the link exercises a small fraction of the 424-row catalogue.

Declared as a field-level audit trail for changes to findings — recording which field moved from what value to what, why, and by whom — but it holds 0 rows. It was created and indexed but never written to, so finding history has no record here.

Links findings to the verses they rest on, distinguishing the anchor verse from supporting ones. The table is small and lopsided: 3,586 of 3,659 rows are 'anchor' rows that carry only a textual reference and no verse_record_id, while the 73 'SUPPORT' rows are the only ones actually resolved to a verse record.

The live meaning-keyed inner-being characteristic index: one row per distinct sense of a Hebrew term as read in a book, keyed on lemma plus English reading rather than on the lemma alone. 1,634 rows, all provenance 'ib-char-index-v3-meaning-keyed-2026' and all status 'surfaced', covering only Psalms (877) and Proverbs (757). Seven columns inherited from the older registry shape are 100% NULL.

A small transitional store of 81 observations from the fan-out reads of nine focus verses (chiefly Lev 25:43, Exo 1:13 and Gen 6:5), each tying a dimension to a term anchor with a narrative. Per the method reset these fold into ve_lexical items; the store is not linked to the lexical tables and covers only a handful of verses.

Maps 1,717 Strong's lemmas to the inner-being faculty or faculties they engage (affect, cognition, volition, moral evaluation and combinations), with a stated basis and a confidence. Machine-generated in a single run on 2026-06-24 under model faculty-map-v1: every row shares one model version and one timestamp, so the whole table is one pass with no incremental maintenance since.

A flat reference lexicon of 11,666 Strong's entries harvested wholesale from STEP on 2026-06-16 — original-script lemma, transliteration, gloss, medium definition and corpus occurrence count. It is a background reference covering the whole biblical vocabulary, not just the study's terms, and is independent of mti_terms (which indexes only 4,221 distinct Strong's).

Records the registry words that reference a term other than its owning one — the XREF side of term ownership, held as a junction between mti_terms and word_registry. Small at 462 rows over 279 terms, and skewed to affect vocabulary (wrath, sorrow, terror), so it maps only a fraction of the cross-referencing implied by the ~3,380 XREF rows in wa_term_inventory.

Junction attaching Phase 2 triage flags from phase2_flag_types to terms in mti_terms; 1,005 assignments across 785 terms. In practice it uses a very narrow slice of the flag vocabulary — 994 of the 1,005 rows are just GOD_AS_SUBJECT and SOMATIC_INNER_LINK.

The many-to-many placement of terms into cluster sub-groups, replacing the old single-valued column on mti_terms. 1,196 placements over 740 distinct terms, so a term can sit in several sub-groups, with the placement note distinguishing primary from secondary. 173 placements are delete-flagged.

The master term index: one row per Hebrew/Greek/Aramaic term drawn into the study, carrying the term's identity (Strong's, transliteration, gloss, language), which English registry word owns it, its extraction status and its Verse Context progress. Intended as one row per Strong's, but the data does not bear that out: 7,861 rows cover only 4,221 distinct Strong's numbers, and the 5,131 delete-flagged rows still repeat 2,567 Strong's; only the 2,730 live rows are genuinely one-per-Strong's. Extraction dates cluster in March 2026, so the bulk of the table is an early-programme intake that has since been pruned by flagging rather than deletion.

The passage register (4,296 rows): a passage is a maximal run of consecutive verses forming the reading unit, anchored on its first verse. Notably no passage crosses a chapter boundary (start_chapter equals end_chapter on all 4,296 rows), so passages are chapter-bounded in practice. Referenced by verse.passage_id, though no FK is declared in either direction.

Lookup of the 25 Phase 2 flag codes an analyst may raise against a term, each with a prose definition of when it applies — e.g. thin datasets, God as subject of an inner state, or cross-testament pairs. A clean, small controlled list: every code and every description is distinct.

The DB-canonical store of authored prose: one row per titled section of narrative — chapter readings, cluster essays, synthesis passages and programme documentation — with its full body text, version lineage and approval state. Almost all of it is machine-authored (claude_code or claude_ai); exactly one row is attributed to the researcher.

Declared as a many-to-many link between prose sections and dimensions, with a link_type qualifying the relationship, but it holds 0 rows. It was created, keyed and uniquely indexed, and never used — a plausible casualty of the dimension layer's retirement.

Declared as a many-to-many link between prose sections and findings, so that a passage could be traced to the evidence behind it, but it holds 0 rows. Its FK points at the legacy wa_session_b_findings rather than the live finding table, so it was superseded before it was ever populated.

An FTS5-managed shadow table holding the inverted index itself as opaque binary segment blobs. It is SQLite internal machinery — the contents are not human-readable and must never be written or interpreted directly; the index is maintained automatically as prose_section changes.

An FTS5-managed shadow table recording, per indexed document, the token count of each column in a packed binary form. FTS5 uses it for relevance ranking; it is internal machinery with one row per prose_section row.

An FTS5-managed shadow table mapping index segments and term prefixes to the pages within prose_section_fts_data where their postings live — the b-tree lookup layer of the index. Internal machinery; the 'term' values are binary prefix keys, not words from the prose.

The controlled vocabulary of prose section kinds — 108 codes spanning programme documentation, per-session outputs, cluster findings and lexical prose — each with a label, the stage that produces it, and expected length bounds. The chapter-by-chapter worklist for the Psalms re-read, one row per chapter with the gate counts recorded at completion. It is single-purpose and finished: all 150 rows are book 19 (Psalms), all provenance 'reread-psalms-2026', and all status 'done'.

Migration ledger: one row per schema version applied to the database, each carrying the cumulative migration history as JSON. 16 rows spanning 3.15.0 to later versions, written between April and the present — it is an append-only audit trail, not a single-row current-version marker.

Reading segments above the verse: 877 named units of text (a thread, discourse or scene) each summarised by the characteristics it carries and a gist. Coverage is narrow and uneven — only 22 books appear, with Proverbs (323) and Job (101) dominating — so this is a partially rolled-out layer, not a canon-wide segmentation. 89 rows are soft-deleted.

The membership junction resolving each segment_unit to its verses (11,276 rows over 877 units and 10,330 distinct verses). Verses can belong to more than one unit — 11,276 memberships against 10,330 verses — which is consistent with threads overlapping bounded segments.

Declared and never used: 0 rows. Part of the four-table Session D scaffolding, intended to hold observations raised by a Session D run (typed, with implicated registries/terms and a gate). Holds collection-level lexical judgements about a term — properties asserted of the term across its whole verse set rather than in any one verse (mutability, transitivity, object type, valence register, membership scope, faculty). Per-Strong's-number record of STEP API fetches (2,377 rows), showing what was requested, what it resolved to, and how many verses came back and were stored. Declared as a lookup of thematic labels but has 0 rows — created and never used. Nothing in the live model links to it; theme-like grouping is done through the cluster and characteristic tables instead.

The many-to-many link between verse-context groups and terms, replacing the old single mti_term_id column on verse_context_group. Notably 3,093 of 5,091 rows are delete-flagged — more than are live — so the majority of this table is retired M47-backfill history rather than current membership.

A 33-row scratch tracker for the fan-out reading of a small researcher-curated verse set (fear-of-God versus oppression of the dependent), recording which verses were reached, by which observation, and on which dimensions. Its cross-reference targets are just two verses (Exo 1:13 and Lev 25:43), so it tracks one narrow investigation from late June 2026, not the programme's reading state.

The term-in-verse classification record (55,775 rows): for one verse-record and one MTI term it holds whether that occurrence is relevant to the study, which verse-context group and cluster subgroup it belongs to, and the L1/L2 verse-read fields (keywords, analysis note, meaning). Unique on (verse_record_id, mti_term_id, group_id, cluster_subgroup_id). Several columns declared for a sense/pole model were never populated.

The catalogue of verse-context groups (VCGs) — named groupings of term-in-verse occurrences that share a context, referenced by verse_context.group_id. Only 1,088 of the 4,155 rows are live: 3,067 (74%) are soft-deleted, mostly by two documented bulk clearances in May 2026.

A derived, materialised roll-up of study coverage per verse — how many spans, study terms and lexical units each verse carries, and whether it is in scope. It is a stale snapshot: all 23,593 rows were built at one instant on 2026-06-27 and it covers verse_id 1..23593 only, so 2,041 of the master table's 25,634 verses are absent. The scope_basis column itself declares the underlying anchor 'debunked'.

A per-word morphology extract for a narrow set of verses — 2,877 word rows covering only 326 distinct references, concentrated in Leviticus, Proverbs and Galatians. It duplicates the shape of verse_morphology on a tiny subset, so it reads as a pilot or one-off working extract from a batch of runs on 2026-06-28 rather than a maintained table.

column3: no declared primary key — see cfg_column for verse_evidence_index's real columns
column4: The fan-in index that answers 'what evidence is bound to this verse' — 804,805 rows mapping a verse to each piece of evidence held against it, so a verse's full raw data can be retrieved in one query. It is a derived index over the other stores, not an authoring surface.

column3: no declared primary key — see cfg_column for verse_evidence_orphan's real columns
column4: The reject log of the verse_evidence_index build: 222 evidence rows that could not be bound to a verse. Every row has the same single cause, making this a small, specific integrity backlog rather than a general error table.

A derived per-verse syntactic complexity profile counting content words, finite and non-finite verbs, conjunctions, prepositions and subordinators, with a summary score. Like verse_coverage it is a frozen snapshot — all 23,593 rows share one build timestamp of 2026-06-27 and cover verse_id 1..23593, i.e. 2,041 verses short of the master table.

The morphological backbone of the layer: one row per word of every verse (325,507 rows), carrying the surface form, Strong's tag, morph_code and the language/pos/stem derived from it. Unique on (verse_id, word_index) and sourced entirely from STEP. verse_span_index is a near-identical copy of this table plus analytical columns.

The raw STEP HTML behind the parsed morphology — one row per verse (25,634, i.e. complete cover of the master verse table), kept so the parse in verse_morphology can be re-derived or audited without re-fetching. This is an archival payload store, not a query surface.

The working analytical surface over word spans (325,474 rows): it reproduces verse_morphology's columns almost exactly and adds the analytical overlay — role, characteristic candidacy, ib_char link and cluster. The duplication is substantial and worth noting: source='verse_morphology' on every row confirms it is a materialised copy, and its row count sits 33 short of the source, so the two can drift.

column3: no declared primary key — see cfg_column for verse_term_index's real columns
column4: A minimal derived lookup of which Strong's terms appear in which verse (275,593 rows, no primary key, indexed both ways). It is a de-duplicated projection of verse_morphology's (verse_id, primary_strong) pairs — a fast reverse index for 'which verses contain this term', holding no data of its own.

A one-off audit artefact: 22 observations from the April 2026 global-rules audit, each recording a problem with a rule and where its content should migrate. Entirely historical — all 22 rows are marked obsolete with an identical reason, yet all 22 still show migration_status 'pending', so the record contradicts itself.

158 researcher-authored links between registry words, each naming the connecting Hebrew or Greek term and explaining the connection in prose — the pre-cluster way of recording that, say, anguish and grief share vocabulary. Superseded by the cluster model but retained; 140 of the 158 rows date from a single 2026-03-16 load and only 6 have been touched since.

The 11 kinds of relationship that may connect two registry words, e.g. shared root, semantic opposition, causative chain. It is the controlled vocabulary behind wa_cross_registry_links.connection_type_id, though the link table belongs to the pre-cluster era.

Engine-derived data-quality evidence raised against a term in a word-study file (19,866 rows) — automated observations such as thin verse coverage or a concrete/physical gloss. All rows resolve to just 7 flag types, and the table has no resolution or soft-delete column, so it is an append-only log with no lifecycle.

A completion log for the retired dimension review: one row per C-code cluster finished, six in all (C10, C13, C17, C20, C21, C22), recorded between 2026-04-09 and 2026-05-02. Against the 22 C-codes present in wa_dimension_index it shows the review was closed out for only six clusters before the layer was abandoned.

The retired dimension-review layer: 3,509 rows, one per verse_context_group, recording which of 20 named dimensions the group was assigned to and how its verses were triaged into anchor, related and set-aside. Written between 2026-04-06 and 2026-05-02 under the C-code cluster scheme and not touched since; superseded by the M-code cluster and finding model.

One row per input file (or engine onboarding stub) that supplied a registry word's data, with the file's provenance, split-part structure and specification version. CLAUDE.md marks it legacy — joins should use the bypass FK word_registry_fk rather than routing through this table — and its metadata columns are inconsistently filled across the eras it spans.

The 23 registered filename conventions used across the programme, each given as a template such as 'wa-dim-{cluster}-extract-{YYYYMMDD}.json' with the instruction that governs it. It is documentation held as data — nothing enforces these patterns, and the table has been unchanged since its single 2026-04-20 load.

The legacy mapping of Session B findings to catalogue questions, with a coverage judgement and a note on what the finding contributed. It is the predecessor of finding_question_link, points at wa_session_b_findings rather than the live finding table, and was written in April and May 2026; unlike its successor it exercises 375 of the catalogue's questions and records real coverage verdicts.

A legacy link from Session B findings to the verses or verse-context groups they attach to, superseded by finding_verse_link under the live model. Small and closed: 287 rows written across three batch runs in late April 2026, covering only 49 findings, and nothing has been added or deleted since.

Maps quality-flag types to the catalogue questions that a raised flag should prompt, so that a data-quality signal pulls in the right analytical prompts. Tiny and static: twelve rows, all written in one run on 20 April 2026, all connecting four flag types to the Q-COV coverage question family.

The 11 registered identifier formats used for labels rather than filenames — finding ids, flag ids, patch ids, group codes — each mapped to the column it populates. Like wa_file_name_pattern it is documentation-as-data with no enforcement, untouched since its 2026-04-20 load.

Structured parse of the Liddell-Scott-Jones classical Greek lexicon entry for a term, splitting the raw entry into gloss, domains, and philosophical and etymological notes. Barely used: 9 rows against 2,221 inventory terms holding an lsj_entry, and 7 of the 9 are one small set of wealth vocabulary (ploutos and its cognates) done on 2026-05-14 — a pilot, not a programme.

One header row per inventory term for its parsed definition, holding the counts and derived flags of the parse whose detail lives in wa_meaning_sense and wa_meaning_stem. 7,748 rows, one-to-one with the term (term_inv_id is unique). Note the language column is broken: it reads 'Hebrew' for 2,386 rows whose term is actually Greek or Aramaic.

The parsed sense hierarchy of a term's definition: 17,125 rows, one per numbered sense, keyed to wa_meaning_parsed and ordered by the source's own numbering (1, 1a, 1a1 and so on). Three of its columns — stem_label, domain_tag and is_homonym — were designed to enrich the hierarchy and carry no data at all, so the table delivers plain nesting only.

Breaks a Hebrew verb's definition down by verbal stem (Qal, Piel, Hiphil and so on) with the sense each stem carries. Effectively unused: 13 rows covering just 3 terms, against 7,748 parses — the stem layer was built and then abandoned, as wa_meaning_parsed.stem_count being 0 on 7,745 rows confirms.

The observation question catalogue: 424 prompts that drive analysis, organised by tier and component, each with its text, scope, provenance and lifecycle status. Its state is the notable thing — 243 of 424 rows are marked deleted and only 239 are 'active', the residue of a v2 restructure that retired 159 questions as redundant; note also that deleted and status disagree in count, so the two lifecycle markers are not kept consistent.

The 20 recognised JSON patch types, each naming the instruction that governs it and the tables it writes to — the reference-as-database record of what a patch of a given type is allowed to do. Written in April and barely touched since; nothing here has been deprecated.

Records which evidence a given prose section cites — a finding, a Q&A catalogue link, an SD pointer, or an observation sequence — together with the citation marker as it appears in the text. It covers only 25 prose sections out of 1,039 and was written in five batches in late April 2026; all its FKs point at the legacy Session B evidence tables, so it documents the old citation model rather than the live finding store.

Lookup of the 29 data-quality and research flag codes, grouped by kind and each defined in prose. Unlike phase2_flag_types it carries a deprecation mechanism and has been through at least one merge (THIN_DATA folded into VERSE_EVIDENCE_CONCENTRATED), so 4 codes are retired but retained.

The programme's global rules held as data: 59 rules with their text, rationale, application notes and supersession chain, all imported from a single JSON document. It is a live governance record only in the historical sense — 25 of the 59 rules are already marked obsolete and nothing has been written since April.

A near-empty remnant of the Session B per-word dimensional assessment: just 2 rows, for registries 112 and 182, raised on 27 and 28 March 2026 under instruction v5.1/v5.2. Four fixed dimensions were each flagged present with a prose note. The structure was abandoned almost immediately — with two rows it carries no analytical weight and serves only as provenance for the approach.

The superseded per-word Session B findings store: 2,883 findings raised April to May 2026 across 112 registries, since replaced by the universal finding table. It is retained rather than live, and carries its own audit trail — 264 findings were dropped in June 2026 as fabricated or templated, and 983 remain 'pending' with no resolution.

Researcher-facing pointers and findings raised during analysis (715 rows) — a working queue of things to return to, with routing (session_target, cluster_link) and a resolution lifecycle. It has genuine vocabulary drift: priority holds both 'MEDIUM'/'HIGH'/'LOW' and lower-case 'normal'/'advisory', and session_target holds both 'D' and 'Session D', 'B' and 'Session B', 'Researcher' and 'researcher' — the same value spelled several ways with no CHECK to stop it.

The per-registry term inventory: one row per term as held under a given English word's file, carrying the STEP-sourced identity, gloss, meaning text, occurrence count, testament span and — critically — term_owner_type, which marks whether this is the term's canonical home (OWNER) or a cross-reference copy (XREF). At 7,844 rows it parallels mti_terms closely, but it is the registry-facing view: the same Strong's recurs across registries, giving 4,155 distinct Strong's over 7,844 rows.

Junction attaching Phase 2 triage flags from phase2_flag_types to inventory terms: 1,570 assignments over 883 terms, using 25 distinct flag types. Broader in coverage than the parallel mti_term_flags (which uses only four types), but 1,092 of the rows are a single bulk patch dated 2026-03-19, so most of this table is machine-applied rather than assessed.

The related-word web: 103,944 rows attaching each inventory term to other lemmas STEP reports as related, by gloss, transliteration and Strong's. Overwhelmingly a bulk import of STEP's relatedNos field with no editorial layer — of a 34,641-row sample only 105 rows carry any relationship note at all, and none is soft-deleted.

Assigns inventory terms to a shared etymological root family by root code, so terms from one root (e.g. CHARAH, 'burn/anger') can be worked together. 2,861 rows over 2,860 distinct terms — roughly a third of the inventory — grouped into 964 root codes, and mostly backfilled in April 2026 by clustering wa_term_related_words rather than by direct etymological research.

The legacy per-term-in-verse occurrence store (247,046 rows) that predates the master verse table — one row per term found in a verse, with the verse text, context, morphology and cluster/analysis markers denormalised onto it. It remains the anchor for verse_context, but it is heavily encumbered: 171,156 rows (69%) are soft-deleted, verse_id is NULL on some rows (the cause of the verse_evidence_orphan entries), and it duplicates verse_text and morph_code held authoritatively elsewhere.

The junction between a wa_verse_records occurrence and a wa_term_inventory term (237,531 rows), unique on (verse_id, term_inv_id) and carrying the STEP sub-gloss that was matched. Note the naming trap: its verse_id column points at wa_verse_records.id, not at verse.id.

The 39 permitted values across the 8 declared vocabularies, one row per value with its label, description and sort order. It has a full supersession mechanism (deprecated, deprecation_note, superseded_by_member_id) that has never once been used — no value has ever been retired or replaced.

Declares 8 controlled vocabularies (dimension labels, dominant subject, confidence markers, Stage 2c outcomes), naming for each the DB column it governs and the instruction that ratified it. It is the intended enforcement layer for those value sets, but the enforcement is documentary only — no FK or CHECK in the schema points at wa_vocab_member.

The programme's lexical entry point: one row per English inner-life word (222 rows), carrying the word's definition, provenance, cluster assignment and the per-stage status fields that drive the pipeline. It accreted columns across several method eras, so it now mixes live status tracking with abandoned layers (dimension review, spirit-soul-body classification) and several columns that were never filled.

Per-word outcome of each engine run: which phase the word reached, what the audit concluded and why it stopped. 539 rows over 373 runs — the audit's verdict history, and it shows REVIEW (491) as the overwhelming norm against only 8 PASS.
